clauses.normalized_text: This document specifies the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP).
clauses.raw_text: This document specifies the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP).

clauses.normalized_text: TCP is an important transport layer protocol in the Internet protocol stack, and has continuously evolved over decades of use and growth of the Internet.
clauses.raw_text: TCP is an important transport layer protocol in the Internet protocol stack, and has continuously evolved over decades of use and growth of the Internet.

clauses.normalized_text: Over this time, a number of changes have been made to TCP as it was specified in RFC 793, though these have only been documented in a piecemeal fashion.

clauses.normalized_text: This document collects and brings those changes together with the protocol specification from RFC 793.

clauses.normalized_text: TCP provides a reliable, in-order, byte-stream service to applications.
clauses.raw_text: TCP provides a reliable, in-order, byte-stream service to applications.

clauses.normalized_text: The TCP design includes only rudimentary security features that improve the robustness and reliability of connections and application data transfer, but there are no built-in cryptographic capabilities to support any form of privacy, authentication, or other typical security functions.
clauses.raw_text: The TCP design includes only rudimentary security features that improve the robustness and reliability of connections and application data transfer, but there are no built-in cryptographic capabilities to support any form of privacy, authentication, or other typical security functions.

clauses.normalized_text: Non-cryptographic enhancements (e.g. [34]) have been developed to improve robustness of TCP connections to particular types of attacks, but the applicability and protections of non-cryptographic enhancements are limited (e.g. see section 1.1 of [34]).
clauses.raw_text: Non-cryptographic enhancements (e.g. [34]) have been developed to improve robustness of TCP connections to particular types of attacks, but the applicability and protections of non-cryptographic enhancements are limited (e.g. see section 1.1 of [34]).

clauses.normalized_text: Applications typically utilize lower-layer (e.g. IPsec) and upper-layer (e.g. TLS) protocols to provide security and privacy for TCP connections and application data carried in TCP.
clauses.raw_text: Applications typically utilize lower-layer (e.g. IPsec) and upper-layer (e.g. TLS) protocols to provide security and privacy for TCP connections and application data carried in TCP.

clauses.normalized_text: Methods based on TCP options have been developed as well, to support some security capabilities.
clauses.raw_text: Methods based on TCP options have been developed as well, to support some security capabilities.

clauses.normalized_text: In order to fully protect TCP connections (including their control flags) IPsec or the TCP Authentication Option (TCP-AO) [33] are the only current effective methods.
clauses.raw_text: In order to fully protect TCP connections (including their control flags) IPsec or the TCP Authentication Option (TCP-AO) [33] are the only current effective methods.

clauses.normalized_text: Other methods discussed in this section may protect the payload, but either only a subset of the fields (e.g. tcpcrypt [56]) or none at all (e.g. TLS).
clauses.raw_text: Other methods discussed in this section may protect the payload, but either only a subset of the fields (e.g. tcpcrypt [56]) or none at all (e.g. TLS).

clauses.normalized_text: Other
clauses.raw_text: Other

clauses.normalized_text: security features that have been added to TCP (e.g. ISN generation, sequence number checks, and others) are only capable of partially hindering attacks.
clauses.raw_text: security features that have been added to TCP (e.g. ISN generation, sequence number checks, and others) are only capable of partially hindering attacks.

clauses.normalized_text: Applications using long-lived TCP flows have been vulnerable to attacks that exploit the processing of control flags described in earlier TCP specifications [27].
clauses.raw_text: Applications using long-lived TCP flows have been vulnerable to attacks that exploit the processing of control flags described in earlier TCP specifications [27].

clauses.normalized_text: TCP-MD5 was a commonly implemented TCP option to support authentication for some of these connections, but had flaws and is now deprecated.
clauses.raw_text: TCP-MD5 was a commonly implemented TCP option to support authentication for some of these connections, but had flaws and is now deprecated.

clauses.normalized_text: TCP-AO provides a capability to protect long-lived TCP connections from attacks, and has superior properties to TCP-MD5.
clauses.raw_text: TCP-AO provides a capability to protect long-lived TCP connections from attacks, and has superior properties to TCP-MD5.

clauses.normalized_text: It does not provide any privacy for application data, nor for the TCP headers.
clauses.raw_text: It does not provide any privacy for application data, nor for the TCP headers.

clauses.normalized_text: The "tcpcrypt" [56] Experimental extension to TCP provides the ability to cryptographically protect connection data.
clauses.raw_text: The "tcpcrypt" [56] Experimental extension to TCP provides the ability to cryptographically protect connection data.

clauses.normalized_text: Metadata aspects of the TCP flow are still visible, but the application stream is well-protected.
clauses.raw_text: Metadata aspects of the TCP flow are still visible, but the application stream is well-protected.

clauses.normalized_text: Within the TCP header, only the urgent pointer and FIN flag are protected through tcpcrypt.
clauses.raw_text: Within the TCP header, only the urgent pointer and FIN flag are protected through tcpcrypt.

clauses.normalized_text: The TCP Roadmap [45] includes notes about several RFCs related to TCP security.
clauses.raw_text: The TCP Roadmap [45] includes notes about several RFCs related to TCP security.

clauses.normalized_text: Many of the enhancements provided by these RFCs have been integrated into the present document, including ISN generation, mitigating blind in-window attacks, and improving handling of soft errors and ICMP packets.
clauses.raw_text: Many of the enhancements provided by these RFCs have been integrated into the present document, including ISN generation, mitigating blind in-window attacks, and improving handling of soft errors and ICMP packets.

clauses.normalized_text: These are all discussed in greater detail in the referenced RFCs that originally described the changes needed to earlier TCP specifications.
clauses.raw_text: These are all discussed in greater detail in the referenced RFCs that originally described the changes needed to earlier TCP specifications.

clauses.normalized_text: Additionally, see RFC 6093 [35] for discussion of security considerations related to the urgent pointer field, that has been deprecated.
clauses.raw_text: Additionally, see RFC 6093 [35] for discussion of security considerations related to the urgent pointer field, that has been deprecated.

clauses.normalized_text: Since TCP is often used for bulk transfer flows, some attacks are possible that abuse the TCP congestion control logic.
clauses.raw_text: Since TCP is often used for bulk transfer flows, some attacks are possible that abuse the TCP congestion control logic.

clauses.normalized_text: An example is "ACK-division" attacks.
clauses.raw_text: An example is "ACK-division" attacks.

clauses.normalized_text: Updates that have been made to the TCP congestion control specifications include mechanisms like Appropriate Byte Counting (ABC) [23] that act as mitigations to these attacks.
clauses.raw_text: Updates that have been made to the TCP congestion control specifications include mechanisms like Appropriate Byte Counting (ABC) [23] that act as mitigations to these attacks.

clauses.normalized_text: Other attacks are focused on exhausting the resources of a TCP server.
clauses.raw_text: Other attacks are focused on exhausting the resources of a TCP server.

clauses.normalized_text: Examples include SYN flooding [26] or wasting resources on non-progressing connections [37].
clauses.raw_text: Examples include SYN flooding [26] or wasting resources on non-progressing connections [37].

clauses.normalized_text: Operating systems commonly implement mitigations for these attacks.
clauses.raw_text: Operating systems commonly implement mitigations for these attacks.

clauses.normalized_text: Some common defenses also utilize proxies, stateful firewalls, and other technologies outside of the end-host TCP implementation.
clauses.raw_text: Some common defenses also utilize proxies, stateful firewalls, and other technologies outside of the end-host TCP implementation.

clauses.normalized_text: The IPv4 specification [1] includes a precedence value in the (now obsoleted) Type of Service field (TOS) field.
clauses.raw_text: The IPv4 specification [1] includes a precedence value in the (now obsoleted) Type of Service field (TOS) field.

clauses.normalized_text: It was modified in [16], and then obsoleted by the definition of Differentiated Services (DiffServ) [5].
clauses.raw_text: It was modified in [16], and then obsoleted by the definition of Differentiated Services (DiffServ) [5].

clauses.normalized_text: Setting and conveying TOS between the network layer, TCP implementation, and applications is obsolete, and replaced by DiffServ in the current TCP specification.
clauses.raw_text: Setting and conveying TOS between the network layer, TCP implementation, and applications is obsolete, and replaced by DiffServ in the current TCP specification.

clauses.normalized_text: RFC 793 requires checking the IP security compartment and precedence on incoming TCP segments for consistency within a connection, and with application requests.
clauses.raw_text: RFC 793 requires checking the IP security compartment and precedence on incoming TCP segments for consistency within a connection, and with application requests.

clauses.normalized_text: Each of these aspects of IP have become outdated, without specific updates to RFC 793.
clauses.raw_text: Each of these aspects of IP have become outdated, without specific updates to RFC 793.

clauses.normalized_text: The issues with precedence were fixed by [20], which is Standards Track, and so this present TCP specification includes those changes.
clauses.raw_text: The issues with precedence were fixed by [20], which is Standards Track, and so this present TCP specification includes those changes.

clauses.normalized_text: However, the state of IP security options that may be used by MLS systems is not as clean.

clauses.raw_text: Resetting connections when incoming packets do not meet expected security compartment or precedence expectations has been recognized

clauses.normalized_text: as a possible attack vector [54], and there has been discussion about amending the TCP specification to prevent connections from being aborted due to non-matching IP security compartment and DiffServ codepoint values.
clauses.raw_text: as a possible attack vector [54], and there has been discussion about amending the TCP specification to prevent connections from being aborted due to non-matching IP security compartment and DiffServ codepoint values.

clauses.normalized_text: In DiffServ the former precedence values are treated as Class Selector codepoints, and methods for compatible treatment are described in the DiffServ architecture.
clauses.raw_text: In DiffServ the former precedence values are treated as Class Selector codepoints, and methods for compatible treatment are described in the DiffServ architecture.

clauses.normalized_text: The RFC 793/1122 TCP specification includes logic intending to have connections use the highest precedence requested by either endpoint application, and to keep the precedence consistent throughout a connection.
clauses.raw_text: The RFC 793/1122 TCP specification includes logic intending to have connections use the highest precedence requested by either endpoint application, and to keep the precedence consistent throughout a connection.

clauses.normalized_text: This logic from the obsolete TOS is not applicable for DiffServ, and should not be included in TCP implementations, though changes to DiffServ values within a connection are discouraged.
clauses.raw_text: This logic from the obsolete TOS is not applicable for DiffServ, and should not be included in TCP implementations, though changes to DiffServ values within a connection are discouraged.

clauses.normalized_text: The obsoleted TOS processing rules in TCP assumed bidirectional (or symmetric) precedence values used on a connection, but the DiffServ architecture is asymmetric.
clauses.raw_text: The obsoleted TOS processing rules in TCP assumed bidirectional (or symmetric) precedence values used on a connection, but the DiffServ architecture is asymmetric.

clauses.normalized_text: Problems with the old TCP logic in this regard were described in [20] and the solution described is to ignore IP precedence in TCP.

clauses.normalized_text: TCP is used by many applications that have a request-response style of communication, where the combination of the Nagle algorithm and delayed acknowledgements can result in poor application performance.
